source.english_context: Unit 15 Safety, Weather, and Everyday Problems Goal: stay safe at home and outside, understand alerts, and ask for urgent help. Daily Life English Is this a safe area to walk at night? The smoke alarm is beeping. There is a power outage. I need help, but it is not an emergency. Where is the nearest exit? Can you help me read this weather alert? Where is the meeting point outside? The sidewalk is very icy. Is there a shelter nearby? I smell gas in the hallway. The front door will not lock. Could you call for help? Which number should I call about this problem? Do you know when the power will return? I cannot find my phone charger. Vocabulary smoke alarm a device that warns about smoke or fire power outage when electricity stops working weather alert a warning about dangerous weather non-emergency number a police or city number for problems that are not urgent shelter a safe place during danger flashlight a small light you hold in your hand exit a way out of a building or place first-aid kit a set of basic supplies for minor injuries evacuation the act of leaving a place because of danger meeting point a place where people agree to gather icy covered with ice charger a device that supplies power to a battery US Customs Call 911 for fire, serious danger, or urgent medical problems. For non-urgent problems, use a local non-emergency number or building manager. Keep basic supplies: water, medicine, flashlight, chargers, and copies of documents. Dialogue Dispatcher: 911. What is your emergency? Student: There is a fire in my building. Dispatcher: What is your address? Student: 45 Pine Avenue, Apartment 2A. Dispatcher: Leave the building if you can do so safely.

japanese_explanation.heading: 緊急と非緊急を分ける
points: 火事、重大なけが、命の危険、犯罪が進行中なら911です。住所、何が起きたか、自分の名前を言います。
騒音、軽いトラブル、なくした物などは、地域の非緊急番号、管理人、市役所などが合う場合があります。
災害に備えて、水、薬、充電器、懐中電灯、重要書類のコピーを用意しておくと安心です。

existing_simplified_chinese.heading: 分清紧急和非紧急
points: 火灾、严重受伤、生命危险或正在发生的犯罪，要拨打911。先说地址，再说发生了什么和你的名字。
噪音、轻微问题或丢东西，可能更适合联系非紧急电话、楼管或市政府服务。
为灾害准备水、药、充电器、手电筒和重要文件复印件，会更安心。

ja.heading: 緊急と非緊急を分ける
points: 火事、重大なけが、命の危険、犯罪が進行中なら911です。住所、何が起きたか、自分の名前を言います。
騒音、軽いトラブル、なくした物などは、地域の非緊急番号、管理人、市役所などが合う場合があります。
災害に備えて、水、薬、充電器、懐中電灯、重要書類のコピーを用意しておくと安心です。

ko.heading: 긴급 상황과 비긴급 상황 구분하기
points: 화재, 심각한 부상, 생명 위협 또는 범죄가 진행 중일 때는 911에 전화하십시오. 주소, 발생한 상황, 그리고 본인의 이름을 말해야 합니다.
소음, 경미한 문제, 분실물 등은 지역의 비긴급 전화번호, 건물 관리인 또는 시청에 연락하는 것이 적절할 수 있습니다.
재난에 대비하여 물, 약, 충전기, 손전등, 중요 서류 사본을 미리 준비해 두면 안심할 수 있습니다.

zh-Hans.heading: 分清紧急与非紧急情况
points: 如果发生火灾、严重受伤、生命危险或正在发生的犯罪，请拨打911。请告知您的地址、发生的事情和您的姓名。
对于噪音、轻微问题或遗失物品等，联系当地的非紧急电话、楼管或市政府服务可能更合适。
为应对灾害，准备好水、药品、充电器、手电筒和重要文件的复印件会更安心。

es.heading: Distinga entre emergencias y situaciones no urgentes
points: Para incendios, lesiones graves, peligro para la vida o un crimen en curso, llame al 911. Diga su dirección, lo que sucede y su nombre.
Para ruidos, problemas menores o cosas perdidas, puede ser apropiado contactar el número local de no emergencias, al administrador del edificio o al ayuntamiento.
Para prepararse ante desastres, tener agua, medicamentos, cargadores, linternas y copias de documentos importantes le dará tranquilidad.

pt-BR.heading: Diferencie emergências de não emergências
points: Em caso de incêndio, ferimentos graves, perigo de vida ou crime em andamento, ligue para o 911. Informe seu endereço, o que está acontecendo e seu nome.
Para ruídos, problemas menores ou itens perdidos, pode ser apropriado entrar em contato com o número de não emergência local, o gerente do prédio ou a prefeitura.
Para se preparar para desastres, ter água, medicamentos, carregadores, lanternas e cópias de documentos importantes pode trazer tranquilidade.

fr.heading: Distinguer les urgences des situations non urgentes
points: En cas d'incendie, de blessure grave, de danger de mort ou de crime en cours, composez le 911. Indiquez votre adresse, ce qui se passe et votre nom.
Pour le bruit, les problèmes mineurs ou les objets perdus, il peut être approprié de contacter le numéro de non-urgence local, le gérant de l'immeuble ou la mairie.
Pour vous préparer aux catastrophes, avoir de l'eau, des médicaments, des chargeurs, des lampes de poche et des copies de documents importants peut vous rassurer.

de.heading: Notfälle und nicht-dringende Situationen unterscheiden
points: Bei Bränden, schweren Verletzungen, Lebensgefahr oder einem laufenden Verbrechen rufen Sie 911 an. Nennen Sie Ihre Adresse, was passiert ist und Ihren Namen.
Für Lärm, kleinere Probleme oder verlorene Gegenstände ist es möglicherweise passender, die lokale Nicht-Notrufnummer, den Hausverwalter oder die Stadtverwaltung zu kontaktieren.
Um auf Katastrophen vorbereitet zu sein, gibt es Ihnen Sicherheit, Wasser, Medikamente, Ladegeräte, Taschenlampen und Kopien wichtiger Dokumente bereitzuhalten.
